blocks.body: RF has to leave the radio, pass a connector and a feed line, and reach an antenna before it is a radio wave. Foundations Lab 06 matched a length and watched SWR. This lab is the path around that antenna. A bad reading here is a teaching case, not a diagnosis of every real station.

config.intro: Assemble the station RF path from the radio outward.
config.wrong: Start at the radio. The antenna is the far end of this path.
config.doneText: The path is radio, connector, feed line, a matching check, antenna, then the RF path into space.

steps.label: CONNECTOR
steps.note: A connector joins the radio to the cable. A poor one can waste power or make a bad match.

steps.label: FEED LINE
steps.note: Coaxial cable is the usual feed line here. It carries RF. It also loses some of it.

steps.label: MATCHING / MEASUREMENT
steps.note: An SWR or power check belongs in the path before you blame the whole radio.

steps.label: ANTENNA
steps.note: The antenna couples RF to space. Polarization, placement, and aim matter.

steps.label: RF PATH
steps.note: After the antenna, the energy is in the radio path toward other stations.

blocks.body: Feed-line loss in this lab is a relative educational model. Longer cable generally loses more. Loss also changes with frequency and with the kind of cable. The number is not manufacturer data.
Each case is one fault in the path. Fix that fault. Do not treat the case as a complete repair manual.

config.doneText: You separated connector, loss, match, polarization, aim, and placement.

scenes.prompt: The SWR was fine yesterday. Today the connector at the radio is loose and corroded. What is the first path problem?

choices.label: A poor connector
choices.why: The connector is part of the RF path. A bad one can look like a bad antenna.

choices.label: The transmitter power supply
choices.why: Nothing in the case points at the supply. The new fault is the connector.

scenes.prompt: Someone replaced a short feed line with a long run of poor cable, and the distant station got weaker. Power is unchanged.

choices.label: Excessive feed-line loss
choices.why: Length and cable quality changed the loss. The transmitter setting did not.

choices.label: The station changed frequency by accident
choices.why: The case changed the cable, not the dial.

scenes.prompt: SWR is high. A dummy load in place of the antenna brings the reading down. The cable checks out.

choices.label: The antenna is a poor match
choices.why: Replacing the antenna with a dummy load changed the reading, so the mismatch is at the antenna.

choices.label: The radio cannot transmit
choices.why: The dummy-load reading says the radio can still deliver RF into a proper load.

scenes.prompt: A local FM station is strong for other people. Your antenna is horizontal and theirs is vertical.

choices.label: Correct the polarization
choices.why: Matching vertical to vertical improves coupling in the model. It is not the only cause of a weak signal.

choices.label: Raise transmitter power until polarization stops mattering
choices.why: Power does not rotate the antenna.

scenes.prompt: A directional antenna is pointed away from the station you want.

choices.label: Aim it toward that station
choices.why: Gain in this lab is energy pointed one way. Aim uses that redistribution.

choices.label: Swap it for a longer feed line
choices.why: More cable does not aim the antenna.

scenes.prompt: You are choosing a portable VHF setup in a valley parking lot beside a metal building.

choices.label: A short feed line, a vertical antenna, and a clearer spot if you can get one
choices.why: Less loss, matching polarization for local FM, and a less blocked location are the sensible combination.

choices.label: The longest cable you own, laid through the building
choices.why: That adds loss and keeps the antenna in a poor place.

blocks.prompt: Why can changing the antenna system improve a signal even when transmitter power stays exactly the same?
blocks.reference: The transmitter power is what leaves the radio. The connector, feed line, match, polarization, aim, and placement decide how much of that energy arrives usefully. A shorter or better feed line loses less. A matched antenna reflects less. A directional antenna aims more of the same energy toward the station. None of that requires a bigger transmitter.
blocks.unsure: Look at the loss model and the directional antenna. The power setting never moved. The path and the aim did.

blocks.body: RADIO LAB PRACTICE. These questions are about the path you assembled. They are not official exam questions.

blocks.label: RADIO LAB PRACTICE
blocks.notice: Original practice about feed lines, SWR, polarization, and patterns. Not official exam questions.

questions.stem: Which order matches the station path in this lab?
choices: Radio, connector, feed line, matching check, antenna
Antenna, then the radio, then the connector
Battery, microphone, speaker
questions.why: RF leaves the radio through the connector and feed line, is checked, and reaches the antenna.

questions.stem: In the educational loss model, what generally increases feed-line loss?
choices: A longer run, a higher frequency, or a poorer cable
A shorter run of better cable at a lower frequency
Leaving the transmitter power setting alone
questions.why: Those three changes raised the relative loss. The number was a comparison, not a datasheet.

questions.stem: SWR is high into the antenna and drops when a dummy load replaces the antenna. Where is the problem?
choices: The antenna match
The receiver volume
The call sign
questions.why: The dummy load is a proper load for a test. The antenna was the piece that changed the reading.

questions.stem: A local FM signal is vertical and your antenna is horizontal. What does this lab expect?
choices: Weaker relative coupling until the orientations match
No effect, because polarization is the only thing that sets signal strength
The feed line reverses polarization by itself
questions.why: Matching orientation improves coupling in the model. Power, distance, and placement still matter.

questions.stem: What does antenna gain mean in this lab?
choices: Energy is aimed more in some directions and less in others
The transmitter creates extra watts because the antenna is directional
A longer feed line adds gain
questions.why: The directional pattern redistributed the same transmitter power. Aiming toward the station used that pattern.

questions.stem: A connector that was solid yesterday is loose today, and the match looks bad. What failed in the path?
choices: The connector
The operator's call sign
The squelch setting
questions.why: The connector is a stage in the RF path. Squelch does not create SWR.

questions.stem: Which portable arrangement fits the valley case?
choices: A short feed line, vertical polarization, and a clearer location if you can reach one
The longest poor cable, routed through a metal building
A horizontal antenna aimed at the ground
questions.why: That choice cuts loss, matches typical local FM polarization, and avoids the blocked location.

blocks.body: Configure a portable VHF station for a simulated summit. Choose the feed line, orientation, placement, and the SWR check. Do not pick a product brand.

config.doneText: The summit plan uses a short feed line, a vertical antenna in the clear, and an SWR check. Transmitter power was not the fix.

scenes.prompt: You can carry either a short run of reasonable cable or a long coil of poor cable.

choices.label: Use the short run
choices.why: Less length means less loss in the model, which matters when the station is small.

choices.label: Use the long poor coil because it looks like more antenna
choices.why: Feed line is not antenna gain. Extra poor cable loses more.

scenes.prompt: The summit plan is local FM, which you have been treating as vertical.

choices.label: Orient the antenna vertical
choices.why: Match the polarization you expect. It is still not the only factor in the contact.

choices.label: Lay the antenna flat because the summit is high
choices.why: Height does not replace orientation.

scenes.prompt: One spot is beside a rock face. Another is the open side of the summit.

choices.label: Place the antenna on the open side
choices.why: Placement changes the path. The rock face is the poorer of the two sites.

choices.label: Put the antenna inside a metal case to protect it
choices.why: The antenna has to couple to space. A metal box is a poor location.

scenes.prompt: Before you call, the SWR reading is high.

choices.label: Check the connector, feed line, and antenna match before raising power
choices.why: High SWR means reflected power. More transmitter power does not repair the path.

choices.label: Ignore it and double the power
choices.why: The power setting was never the measurement that failed.
